code.originalText: Thirteen-week review: grief therapy, smoking, a gout flare while away, the urate and lipid results

text.paragraph: Thirteen-week review: grief therapy, smoking, a gout flare while away, urate and lipids. [S]

Mr. Clemens returns eight weeks after his five-week review, after nearly three weeks away in August. Two days after he left, his right big toe became hot, swollen and too painful to walk on; a doctor where he was staying prescribed prednisone 40 mg for five days, and he kept taking allopurinol and colchicine as told. The flare settled within a week. Because he was away, the urate test planned three to four weeks after starting allopurinol was not done until today. He stopped smoking on his quit date at the start of August, smoked two cigars one evening while away, and none since; varenicline causes mild nausea only. His bronchitis from the sick visit has cleared. He has had eleven grief therapy sessions, two of them by telephone while away; he missed one. He sleeps about six hours, writes most mornings and has begun to see friends. No chest tightness. [S]
